sheets.rejected_alternative: Five parallel subagents. They lose because subagents only report results back to the caller and never talk to each other, so the required direct adversarial back-and-forth between investigators cannot happen.
sheets.enforcement_owner: The model: the lead session owns coordination, task assignment, and synthesis from natural-language instruction; the harness only provides the teammate spawning, shared task list, and messaging plumbing.
sheets.context_boundary: Each teammate runs in its own fully independent context window; what crosses boundaries is the shared task list, direct teammate-to-teammate messages, and the lead's final synthesis.
sheets.lifecycle: Teammates are spawned when the lead forms the team for this investigation and are cleaned up automatically when the session exits; the debate lives and dies with the session.
sheets.failure_mode: Advisory and fails open: Claude may quietly spawn subagents instead of a real team and the agent panel looks the same, token cost is far higher than a single session, and there are known limitations around session resumption, task coordination, and shutdown behavior.
sheets.version_caveat: Experimental and disabled by default; requires setting CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1 in settings.json or the environment, with the current behavior documented as of v2.1.178.

scenarios.scenario: Our path-based blocks stop the agent's own file tools from reading ~/.aws/credentials and ~/.ssh, but a Python script it launches can still open those files directly. We need every process the agent spawns, including children of children, to be physically unable to read those paths.

key.primary: Enable the Bash sandbox (sandbox.enabled) with sandbox.credentials file entries or sandbox.filesystem.denyRead for the credential paths; Seatbelt on macOS and bubblewrap on Linux/WSL2 enforce the boundary on the process tree
key.rejected_alternative: Read deny rules such as Read(~/.aws/credentials) and Read(~/.ssh/**) in permissions settings
key.rejection_reason: The permissions docs warn that Read and Edit deny rules apply to Claude's built-in file tools and to file commands Claude Code recognizes in Bash, like cat, head, tail, and sed, but not to arbitrary subprocesses that open files themselves, and they point to enabling the sandbox for OS-level enforcement that blocks all processes from accessing a path.
key.context_boundary: no context window (the boundary is an OS-level sandbox enforced at command execution time, blocking all processes rather than just Claude's own tools); the protected credential contents never reach any context, and the boundary holds even when a prompt injection has already steered Claude's decisions
key.lifecycle: OS-level boundary applied to every sandboxed Bash command and all child processes at execution time; subagents inherit the parent session's sandbox configuration
key.failure_mode: No native Windows support; the sandbox's default read policy still permits credential files until you explicitly deny them; and unless allowUnsandboxedCommands is set to false, the dangerouslyDisableSandbox escape hatch can rerun a failing command outside the boundary.
key.version_caveat: Sandbox runs on macOS, Linux, and WSL2 only (not native Windows); the sandbox.credentials block requires v2.1.187 or later

sheets.primary: OS-level sandboxing: enable the sandbox in settings (sandbox.enabled: true) with sandbox.filesystem.denyRead, or the credentials.files grouping, covering ~/.aws/credentials and ~/.ssh. The sandbox is enforced by the operating system and binds every child process of Bash commands, which permission rules cannot do; this is harness settings configuration rather than one of the authored extension mechanisms, and the existing Read deny rules stay on as the complementary layer that merges into the sandbox boundary.
sheets.rejected_alternative: More Read() permission deny rules: already proven insufficient here, because they bind Claude's built-in tools and recognized file commands, not arbitrary subprocesses like the launched Python script.
sheets.enforcement_owner: The harness via the operating system sandbox around the Bash tool; not the model, and not bypassable by prompt injection, since a denied open() fails at the OS layer.
sheets.context_boundary: No context window is involved: the boundary wraps the Bash process tree at the OS level, reads fail inside the child processes themselves, and only the command's error output returns to the model's context.
sheets.lifecycle: Applies to every sandboxed Bash command and all its descendant processes while sandbox.enabled is on; excludedCommands and the dangerouslyDisableSandbox escape hatch run outside it unless allowUnsandboxedCommands is set to false.
sheets.failure_mode: By default it fails open in two places: if the sandbox cannot start (missing dependencies, unsupported platform) commands run unsandboxed with only a warning unless failIfUnavailable is true, and excluded or escape-hatch commands bypass it entirely. It also covers only the Bash tool's process tree, not other tools, so keep the permission deny rules in place.
sheets.version_caveat: Bash sandboxing is available on macOS, Linux and WSL2 only (no native Windows) and is off by default; the credentials.files key requires v2.1.187 or later and filesystem.disabled requires v2.1.216 or later.

sheets.primary: OS-level sandboxing: sandbox.enabled true with filesystem.denyRead entries (or credentials.files deny entries) for ~/.aws/credentials and ~/.ssh; the Seatbelt/bubblewrap boundary applies to every process the Bash tool spawns, children of children included, and Read deny permission rules merge into the same boundary.
sheets.rejected_alternative: Extending the PreToolUse hook or Read deny path rules: those bind only Claude's own tool calls and recognized file commands, not what a spawned Python process does with open(), which is exactly the reported gap.
sheets.enforcement_owner: The harness plus the operating system kernel: enforcement is physical process confinement, not behavioral compliance.
sheets.context_boundary: Applies to the Bash tool's entire process tree in every session; denied bytes can never reach any spawned process, and therefore never reach any context window.
sheets.lifecycle: The sandbox is applied to each Bash command execution while enabled in settings; it stops applying if sandboxing is disabled, the command is in excludedCommands, or the call uses the unsandboxed escape hatch.
sheets.failure_mode: Fails open by default when the platform cannot sandbox (a warning is shown and commands run unsandboxed) unless failIfUnavailable is true; also close the escape hatches by setting allowUnsandboxedCommands false and keeping excludedCommands minimal, or the guarantee has holes.
sheets.version_caveat: Sandboxing covers macOS, Linux, and WSL2 only (no native Windows) and defaults to off; credentials.files and credentials.envVars require v2.1.187+, and failIfUnavailable is intended for managed-settings deployments that need a hard gate.

sheets.primary: OS-level sandboxing rather than any in-harness rule: run the agent's shell under Claude Code's native sandbox (seatbelt on macOS, bubblewrap on Linux) with those paths excluded, or run the whole session in a devcontainer or VM where ~/.aws and ~/.ssh simply are not mounted. Only kernel-level isolation binds children of children.
sheets.rejected_alternative: PreToolUse hooks or permission deny rules: they gate tool calls at the harness boundary and cannot see or constrain what an already-launched process opens at runtime, which is precisely the reported bypass.
sheets.enforcement_owner: Harness plus the OS kernel: the sandbox profile or the container mount table enforces the restriction; the model has no say in it.
sheets.context_boundary: Enforcement lives entirely below the tool layer at the operating system; nothing crosses into the model context except the permission errors that sandboxed processes receive on blocked reads.
sheets.lifecycle: The sandbox wraps each shell invocation (or the entire session in the container case) and is inherited by every descendant process until the process tree exits; it applies for as long as the sandbox configuration or container definition is in force.
sheets.failure_mode: Fails closed inside the sandbox, which can break legitimate tooling that genuinely needs AWS credentials, but fails open wherever the sandbox is unavailable or disabled; platform coverage is the trap, since Windows has no native equivalent and needs WSL2 or a container.
sheets.version_caveat: Native sandboxing for the shell tool is a 2025 addition, platform-gated to macOS seatbelt and Linux bubblewrap and originally behind an opt-in setting or experimental flag whose exact name I do not recall with confidence; container or devcontainer isolation has no version gate.

sheets.primary: Sandboxing: enable the OS-level Bash sandbox in settings (sandbox.enabled true) with filesystem.denyRead or credentials.files entries for ~/.aws/credentials and ~/.ssh, deployed via managed settings. The sandbox boundary applies to Bash commands and their child processes, including children of children, which is what path-based permission rules cannot do.
sheets.rejected_alternative: Read deny permission rules (the current approach): they gate Claude's built-in tools and recognized Bash file commands but do not apply to arbitrary subprocesses like the Python script, which is exactly the observed bypass.
sheets.enforcement_owner: The harness, via the operating system: the sandbox provides OS-level enforcement around every process spawned from the Bash tool, so a spawned interpreter is physically unable to open the paths regardless of what the model does.
sheets.context_boundary: Enforcement happens at the OS process boundary, entirely outside any context window; a blocked read surfaces to the model only as a command error in the Bash tool result. Read deny permission paths are merged into the same sandbox boundary.
sheets.lifecycle: Applies to every sandboxed Bash command while sandbox.enabled is set, merging denyRead paths from all settings scopes; commands in excludedCommands or run via the dangerouslyDisableSandbox escape hatch execute outside it.
sheets.failure_mode: By default it fails open when the sandbox cannot start (missing dependencies or unsupported platform): a warning is shown and commands run unsandboxed, so set failIfUnavailable true and allowUnsandboxedCommands false in managed settings to make it fail closed.
sheets.version_caveat: Sandboxing is platform gated to macOS, Linux, and WSL2 (no native Windows) and is off by default; the credentials.files grouping requires Claude Code v2.1.187 or later.
